title: Ideas Live On
author: Benazir Bhutto
source: Address on Democracy and Human Freedom (2007) / EngageNY Grade 12 Edition
citation: Bhutto, Benazir. 'Ideas Live On.' Address to the Nation, 2007.

sections.heading: Ideas Live On (Address on Democratic Freedom)

epigraph.quote: A man may die, nations may rise and fall, but an idea lives on. Ideas have endurance without death.

paragraphs: I recall that President John F. Kennedy once said that a man may die, nations may rise and fall, but an idea lives on. Ideas have endurance without death. Today, as we stand at this historic crossroad, we reaffirm our conviction that the democratic ideal—the idea that people have the fundamental right to choose their leaders, to live in freedom, and to determine their destiny—cannot be silenced by guns, by prisons, or by exile.

Tyranny and dictatorship are built upon fear. They seek to suppress thought, to crush opposition, and to control the minds of citizens. But fear is an unnatural state for human beings. Deep within every human soul is planted the seed of freedom. No matter how deep the winter of oppression, that seed will eventually break through the frozen soil and reach toward the light.

True stability cannot be achieved through the barrel of a gun or the suspension of constitutions. True stability arises from democratic legitimacy, from the rule of law, from independent judiciaries, and from empowering people through education, healthcare, and economic opportunity. An investment in human dignity is the only lasting defense of a nation.

Throughout my years in exile and political struggle, I have witnessed the immense resilience of the people. Dictators believed that by exiling leaders and banning political assemblies, they could eradicate the democratic movement. But they failed to understand that leaders are merely the servants of an idea. You can exile a person, but you cannot exile an idea whose time has come.

Today, we call for a new dawn: a society rooted in justice, tolerance, pluralism, and fundamental human rights. Let us move forward without fear, united in our determination to build a democratic future worthy of our children and our nation's promise.
